title: RIVET prioritizer: latency-aware portfolio scoring and rollout playbook
creator: Mira Chen
description: Purpose: Introduce a complementary prioritization playbook that explicitly balances latency sensitivity, cost efficiency, uncertainty, and operational throughput. Rationale: existing RICE-derived artifacts emphasize impact and effort; for inference features we need a scoring surface that incorporates real token economics and latency tail risk. RIVET is designed to be applied at initiative and feature-slice level (e.g., 'adaptive batching for chat', 'KV prefetch for long context', 'dedicated autoscaling policy for enterprise pools').
scoring_rubric: RIVET acronym: Response (latency sensitivity), Impact (user/business value), Variance (uncertainty / risk of negative regression), Efficiency (cost per token / tokens saved), Throughput (ops complexity and capacity impact).
Scoring scale: 1-10 for each axis where 10 is highest priority (e.g., Response=10 means very latency sensitive), 1 is lowest.
Default weights: Impact 0.30, Response 0.25, Efficiency 0.20, Variance 0.15 (lower is better -> inverted), Throughput 0.10. We invert Variance score so that high uncertainty reduces overall score.
Normalization: map each raw assessment to 1-10; compute weighted sum. Final score range approximately 1-10. Teams can reweight per cycle for hires or capacity changes.

Guidance for axis assessments: Response: quantify p95/p99 SLO delta or user-facing latency buckets; Impact: align to mapped OKR metric (revenue, DAU retention, conversions); Variance: consider model quality/regression risk, infra unknowns, and data dependencies; Efficiency: estimate tokens/sec or $/1M tokens delta; Throughput: ops maintenance, runbook complexity, scaling constraints.
example_scores: Example initiatives scored to demonstrate prioritization surface:
1) adaptive-batching-v2: Response=7, Impact=8, Variance=4, Efficiency=9, Throughput=6 -> weighted score = 0.25*7 + 0.30*8 + 0.20*9 + 0.15*(10-4) + 0.10*6 = 7.9
2) kv-prefetch-long-context: Response=9, Impact=7, Variance=6, Efficiency=6, Throughput=5 -> weighted score = 0.25*9 + 0.30*7 + 0.20*6 + 0.15*(10-6) + 0.10*5 = 7.55
3) dedicated-autoscale-policy: Response=6, Impact=6, Variance=3, Efficiency=5, Throughput=9 -> weighted score = 0.25*6 + 0.30*6 + 0.20*5 + 0.15*(10-3) + 0.10*9 = 6.55
Interpretation: rank by final score, but apply manual overrides if constraint-bound (e.g., legal, enterprise SLAs).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Decision): Apply RIVET scoring in next roadmap sync across top 12 initiatives and publish scorecard to the console PM channel.

Phase 1 (Experiment): Pick top 3 items for Q2 small-bets: adaptive-batching-v2, kv-prefetch-long-context, lightweight-quantization-probe. Run canary experiments with pre-defined SLO guardrails (p99 latency, regression detection).

Phase 2 (Measure): Use console dashboards to track token economics, p50/p95/p99 latency deltas, unit cost, and objective OKR metrics for 6 weeks. If variance > threshold, open an investigation ticket and lower rollout velocity.

Phase 3 (Scale): Move successful experiments to full rollout via canary/A-B rollouts and add model pinning and fallback policies for safety. Embed rollout policy in release notes and change-log for Dedicated customers when applicable.
okr_mapping: Maps to OKR: Inference Reliability & Economics Q2 2026
Primary OKR: Reduce p99 inference latency for interactive products by 18% and unit token cost by 12% (OKR-IR-2026-Q2),
Secondary OKR: Increase platform throughput for enterprise workloads by 20% under Dedicated pools (OKR-DED-2026-Q2).
